summary: we made project spacelanders to find places on earth that looks and acts like the moon and Mars.before space agencies send astronauts or rovers to other planets, they need to test their gears to know if it would hold up somewhere similar here on earth.some teams use few places that's famous such as the death valley or the Atacama Desert. we used nasa's moon trek,Mars trek, and Earthdata tools to compare the hills,rocks,temps and water resources in new places. our map highlights five great testing parts, including uae's empty  Quarter dunes and salty sabkhas for Mars, plus caves in Iceland and icy ground in Svalbard for the Moon.Finding more testing sites makes space exploration safer and helps teams test equipment closer to home.
details:
Project Spacelanders is an interactive map that pairs five places on Earth with real landing spots on the Moon and Mars. When you click on a spot on our map, you can compare its ground steepness, rocks, weather, and water resources side-by-side with a real lunar or Martian site.

The five Earth spots we picked
  • UAE Empty Quarter (Rub' al Khali) -> Gale Crater (Mars): Huge sand dunes and fine dust make this great for testing rover wheels and solar panels.
  • Abu Dhabi Coastal Sabkhas (UAE) -> Jezero Crater (Mars): These salty, dry flats act like ancient dried-up lakes on Mars, helping scientists test drills and life-finding sensors.
  • Hajar Mountains / Semail Ophiolite (UAE & Oman) -> Nili Fossae (Mars): The dark mantle rocks here match the rocks on the surface of Mars.
  • Raufarhólshellir Lava Tubes (Iceland) -> Marius Hills Pit (Moon): Underground volcanic tunnels can help us test how to build Moon bases protected from space radiation.
  • Svalbard (Norway) -> Shackleton Crater (Moon's South Pole): Freezing frozen ground and low sunlight copy what astronauts will face when looking for ice at the Moon's South Pole.
Factors we considered
To pick good testing spots, we looked at four main things: flat ground for safe landings (under 15 degrees), matching rock and soil types, extreme temperatures and dryness, and hidden water or caves that astronauts could use.
Why it matters and how it helps
Testing space gear is expensive if every team has to travel to the same two or three deserts. By finding new look-alike places around the world, more students and space teams can test rovers, spacesuits, and tools closer to home.
Tools we used
We used NASA Moon Trek, NASA Mars Trek, and NASA Earthdata to compare satellite maps and elevation data, and built our project using My Maps, Canva, and HTML/JavaScript].
